original_question: Let k be a field of characteristic zero. Is the group GAn(k) generated by tame automorphisms together with finitely many one-parameter subgroups of automorphisms?
target_in_paper: Problem 2 (posed by Vladimir Bavula) in the paper's unnumbered list of conference open problems; the notation needed for it appears in the opening notation block on page 1. ([math.ru.nl](https://www.math.ru.nl/~maubach/AAS/Openproblems.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the exact problem the paper states: it asks, for a field k of characteristic zero, whether GA_n(k) is generated by tame automorphisms together with finitely many one-parameter subgroups of automorphisms. This is essentially Problem 2 verbatim, apart from making the notation stand alone. ([math.ru.nl](https://www.math.ru.nl/~maubach/AAS/Openproblems.pdf))
missing_details: The paper leaves the ambient dimension n implicit in the notation GA_n(k); a stand-alone question should fix n (or explicitly quantify over n).
GA_n(k) should be defined explicitly as the group of polynomial k-automorphisms of affine n-space, equivalently Aut_k(k[x_1,...,x_n]).
The tame subgroup should be named explicitly as TA_n(k) and defined using the paper's notation block: it is generated by affine and triangular automorphisms.
The phrase 'finitely many one-parameter subgroups' should be converted into an existence statement such as: there exist H_1,...,H_r with r < infinity such that GA_n(k) = <TA_n(k), H_1,...,H_r>.

The note does not define 'one-parameter subgroup'; to make the question self-contained one should state the intended standard meaning (for example, algebraic one-parameter subgroups of the automorphism group).
refined_question: Fix a positive integer n and let k be a field of characteristic 0. Let GA_n(k) = Aut_k(k[x_1,\dots,x_n]) be the group of polynomial automorphisms of affine n-space A_k^n, and let TA_n(k) \subseteq GA_n(k) be the tame subgroup generated by affine and triangular automorphisms. Do there exist finitely many one-parameter subgroups H_1,\dots,H_r \subseteq GA_n(k) such that GA_n(k) = \langle TA_n(k), H_1,\dots,H_r \rangle?
justification: This arXiv note is not a theorem/proposition paper with a Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3; it is a short unnumbered list of conference open problems. The draft question matches Problem 2 by Vladimir Bavula almost word-for-word. The only nearby context supplied by the paper is the opening notation block, which defines GA_n(C), Aff_n(C), and TA_n(C), and specifies that 'tame' means generated by affine and triangular automorphisms. Hence the paper-faithful refinement is simply to make those implicit notational conventions explicit, without broadening the problem. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.1462))
